claims.statement: prefix: App-level tokens begin with the literal xapp-.

sources.supports: Placeholders only (SLACK_APP_TOKEN='xapp-***', Authorization: Bearer xapp-1-123); the token goes in the Authorization header.

claims.statement: section-structure: After the prefix: a digit section, then three more dash-separated sections (digit, alphanumeric, digit, alphanumeric). (Provider-authored placeholders disagree on whether the version section exists; no provider page states section count. The contract pattern uses this 4-section order with open widths only so positives are well-formed; no twin or control removes the version section or asserts silence on the python-mock order.)

sources.supports: gitleaks SlackAppLevelToken (?i)xapp-\d-[A-Z0-9]+-\d+-[a-z0-9]+, "based on a limited number of examples".
Java SDK socket-mode guide/sample placeholder xapp-1-<A+3>-<3 digits>-<3 x>: version digit first. Placeholder widths are not real.
Contradiction: the python SDK socket-mode mock uses xapp-<A+3>-<3 digits>-<3 lower> with no version section.
internal/goutils/strings_test.go placeholder xapp-1-<A+3>-<4 digits>-<4 upper>.

claims.statement: section-widths: Section widths 1 / 11 / 13 / 64 (97 characters total). (Not frozen. Positives use 1/11/13/64 so they satisfy gitleaks, veles/kingfisher, the product's interim xapp-[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,} floor and Slack CLI's prefix-only redaction; they cannot also satisfy Nosey Parker's 2-section shape, which is recorded, never asserted against: no fixture uses a 42-character xapp- value.)

sources.supports: veles xapp-\d{1,10}-[A-Za-z0-9]{11}-[0-9]{13}-[a-fA-F0-9]{64}; "presumably" hedges the version width.
Kingfisher imports the identical regex (not independent).
Contradiction: np.slack.5 \b(xapp-[0-9]{12}-[a-zA-Z0-9/+]{24})\b — two sections, 42 characters.

claims.statement: alphabet: Section 2 uppercase alphanumeric (app-ID-like); final section lowercase hex. (Not frozen; the pattern accepts any alphanumeric in sections 2 and 4. No fixture twins on tail case or width.)

sources.supports: Case-insensitive; TP samples use lowercase hex tails. Two of three cited samples do not start section 2 with "A", so "section 2 is the App ID" is not consistently supported.
Accepts [a-fA-F0-9] for the tail.

claims.statement: app-id-embedding: Whether section 2 equals the public App ID. (An App ID alone is a public identifier and is used as a public-id control; nothing asserts it is or is not embedded.)

sources.supports: Calls section 2 "an app ID" without a source.
